items.title: `uv lock --check` doesn't error if environment doesn't match lockfile
items.reason: Closest broad command-design discussion. It requests checks across project, lockfile, environment, and hashes; a maintainer clarifies that `uv lock --check` only checks project/lock consistency.

items.title: Validate locked versions against constraints in lock file
items.reason: Directly tracks rejecting corrupted lockfiles whose selected versions violate recorded constraints, but does not validate artifact URLs against fresh index metadata.

items.title: Error on lockfiles with incoherent wheel versions
items.reason: Implemented a narrower structural integrity check for inconsistent package and wheel versions, establishing precedent without providing network-backed provenance verification.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests using literal terms including `uv.lock`, verify, legitimate, tamper, malicious, and URL, plus conceptual queries covering integrity, authenticity, constraints, hashes, artifact provenance, index metadata, refresh, re-resolution, CI, and `uv audit`. Followed the maintainer-linked chain through astral-sh/uv#11932, astral-sh/uv#12276, astral-sh/uv#12254, and astral-sh/uv#12235. No item covers the complete network-backed comparison. astral-sh/uv#18562 repeats the constraint inconsistency covered by astral-sh/uv#12276; astral-sh/uv#18619 is limited to missing hashes for direct/path sdists; astral-sh/uv#18506 concerns vulnerability and malware advisories rather than lockfile provenance.

type_reason: This requests a new independent, network-backed verification capability. Existing checks establish project/lock freshness and verify downloaded bytes against hashes stored in the lockfile, but they do not establish that the lockfile's URL/hash records came from configured-index metadata. No existing item covers the full request.
summary: No exact prior tracker was found. astral-sh/uv#11932 and astral-sh/uv#12276 cover broad check semantics and constraint validation, while astral-sh/uv#12235 added a narrower coherence check; none authenticates artifact provenance against fresh index metadata.
draft_response:
The check you're describing goes beyond `uv lock --check`, which checks whether `uv.lock` is consistent with project metadata rather than independently authenticating every entry against freshly fetched index metadata. During sync, uv verifies downloaded artifacts against the hashes in `uv.lock`, so changing only a wheel URL cannot install different bytes without a hash mismatch. However, the lockfile remains the source of truth for the URL and hash pair.

For CI today, the closest check is `uv lock --refresh` followed by `git diff --exit-code -- uv.lock`. This revalidates index metadata and reports whether uv would regenerate the lockfile differently. The narrower version/constraint check is tracked in astral-sh/uv#12276, while astral-sh/uv#11932 discusses broader check semantics; neither covers the full provenance check requested here. We can keep this issue open to track a dedicated verification workflow and define its guarantees.
